The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1169 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • According to recent reports, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

According to recent reports, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Alongside Picasso, a surprising number of key artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

In a recent development, two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Industry observers note that still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

However, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

Recent findings suggest that the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked massive and dangerous.".

According to recent reports, the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian indicates. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

The designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

It has been revealed that but altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

The feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

"It's really crazy," she claims, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:26.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very important and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical glitch represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In a recent development, in this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He noted: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

Recent findings suggest that what a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich are to travel to Nairobi, Kenya during the winter break to play a friendly that opens the newly finished Raila Odinga International Stadium in the capital city.
  • "Bayern has millions of fantastic fans in Africa with whom we feel a close connection – it's a continent with a huge passion for football," Rouven Kasper, Bayern board member for marketing and sales, said in a club statement.
  • "We will be making a further contribution to raising the profile of the Bundesliga and are very much looking forward to this special event.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich are to travel to Nairobi, Kenya during the winter break to play a friendly that opens the newly finished Raila Odinga International Stadium in the capital city. The German side will face Ajax Amsterdam as the game acts as part of the country's preparations for the 2027 African Cup of Nations (AFCON), which will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania next summer.

"Bayern has millions of fantastic fans in Africa with whom we feel a close connection – it's a continent with a huge passion for football," Rouven Kasper, Bayern board member for marketing and sales, said in a club statement.

"We will be making a further contribution to raising the profile of the Bundesliga and are very much looking forward to this special event.".

It has been revealed that the news is just the latest venture into global sports investing in Africa. Earlier this month, Formula 1 announced it was returning to the continent after Rwanda secured the rights for a deal from the early 2030s onwards. In September, World Athletics revealed Nairobi would host the World Championships in 2029. It will be the first time the event has been held in Africa.

Simon Chadwick, a business management and program director at the African School of Economics, believes that over the last two decades the professionalization and industrialization of sports has begun to emerge in Africa.

"Countries like Rwanda, Kenya, Morocco and obviously, South Africa, if we go back to the last decade of the previous century, have increasingly begun to deploy sport as a policy instrument," Chadwick told DW, adding Senegal and Egypt to the list.

"There are these image and reputational benefits which very often are bundled up as soft power. It's about attractiveness and appeal and engagement," noted Chadwick.

"It's almost like a kind of professionalization, industrialization and politicization of sport that we're seeing elsewhere in the world has now arrived in Africa. We are seeing a much greater sense of kind of self-determination within Africa to do this," he added.

It has been revealed that "This is not just about sport. It is also about diplomacy and bilateral trade, but also about the broader economic and industrial context within which sport sits.".

In a recent development, for Kenya specifically, the building of the stadium is in line with the housing and sports infrastructural development that has been so heavily promoted under President William Ruto. Hosting this game is a symbol of the development currently happening in Nairobi.

"The bigger picture is that Nairobi now is positioning itself as a as an alternative sports venue," Richard Wanjohi, Editorial and Research Lead at the African Sports and Creative Institute (ASCI), told DW.

In a recent development, "I think we have seen what Kigali has done over the last number of years. For us to then come back into this conversation as a major city that can host such an event, it's huge. A few weeks later, we'll have the rugby sevens series again and then ultimately, the Africa Cup of Nations in July.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Chadwick believes that unlike Rwanda, Kenya's relative stability and pre-existing tourist industry allows for a more natural development of sports investment.

"This is not Kenya trying to build a tourism industry through an engagement in sport. I think it's an extension of what Kenya has been doing for a number of years through sport.".

Combined with being a multi-sport country - athletics, rugby, football, volleyball – Wanjohi believes Kenya is ready to make the most of that performance on the field or track.

"It's about time that we also host the world and show them that we can do this from a hosting perspective, but also from developing infrastructure that is ready to host such sports events," Wanjohi noted.

"It's beyond just saying that we have the talent that is already in the sport, but it's saying that we have the infrastructure, we have the skills, we have the capability to host this as any other African, if not global nation.".

However, Ruto's government has been criticized over taxation, unemployment and its handling of dissent. Given that this stadium cost approximately €375 million ($418 million), it is perhaps no surprise that questions are being asked about the decision to invest in major sports infrastructure.

In a recent development, "People are asking, we are a struggling economy. There are a lot of other problems that could be addressed, like the education sector, health and all that. How did we get that money and be able to make that provision? Also interestingly, is that there's an appearance fee that is going to be paid to both Bayern and Ajax," said Wanjohi, who added there was also some frustration that the opening game was not given to local teams or even the national side.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the timing of this also matters. While many sports fans in the country are excited, others are critical.

"The government knows that this is almost like a campaign tool. We have an election coming up in August next year so the government or the president of the day obviously wants to use as much leverage of such an event to milk it for all it's worth," Wanjohi added.

"So the two different schools of thought are: It's a good thing to have, but at what cost are we doing it at and is it in the public interest as well?".

The proof will be in what the legacy of events like Bayern Munich's friendly in Nairobi brings Kenyan football. The feeling in late 2026 though, is largely optimistic.

"I guess the acid test is that many African nations carry with them the baggage from the past that this is just trophy asset investment that is ultimately going to create white, white elephant infrastructure," Chadwick stated.

"But having spoken to people in Kenyan sport, in the industry itself, it seems to me that there is a genuine appetite for sports to become a genuine and legitimate driver of economic activity.".

Janek Speight contributed reporting for this article.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence.
  • Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow.
  • It has been revealed that exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

It has been revealed that exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

Grande chiusura di Sutalo, fondamentale.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.

Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies: Who has won more honours?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1249 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.
  • In a recent development, liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs.
  • With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.

In a recent development, liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so highlights the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

In a recent development, for every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the new head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world reveals where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

Zinedine Zidane therefore took the opportunity to call Senny Mayulu, summoned for the first time to the Blues, who was then part of the Espoirs group at Clairefontaine. The Parisian has the advantage of versatility, as the coach highlighted yesterday.

“It’s a source of pride as a young player to be called up by the A’s of the French team, for the country in which I grew up. I was with the Espoirs in the building next door and the coach warned me that I had to go up with the A’s. Now I have to show why I’m here», Reacted the 20-year-old player in front of an FFF camera, not really impressed by the news. “I’ll fit in well, I already know a lot of people. Everything will be fine, then we have to do the work on the ground. We’re going to travel to Italy, and then I think there will be a little hazing.».

#25910. A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3880 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

#25909. PSG: Ferran Torres, a shortage which is seriously starting to worry

PSG: Ferran Torres, a shortage which is seriously starting to worry

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (602 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Frenchfootballweekly

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are evenings which only accentuate doubts.
  • It has been revealed that the Trojan evening did not allow Ferran Torres to smile again.
  • As a reminder, his last goal dates back to September 20, during the victory against Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are evenings which only accentuate doubts. The one experienced by Ferran Torres against Troyes on Saturday evening is undoubtedly one of them. In a meeting where Paris Saint-Germain ended up finding the fault to win (1-0), the Spanish striker, aligned in a right winger role, once again went through the debates without managing to be sufficiently decisive. However, there was no shortage of opportunities and opportunities to find the net presented themselves to him. But as too often in recent weeks, the last gesture was lacking. A new frustrating performance which extends a worrying period of scarcity for a player whose offensive efficiency is nevertheless one of the main missions.

It has been revealed that the Trojan evening did not allow Ferran Torres to smile again. From the 38th minute of play, the Spaniard came up against Hillel Konaté in a tight angle, before missing two new opportunities just before the break, in the 45th and 45th+2. In the second half, the scenario repeated itself: served by Fabián Ruiz in the 67th minute, he again saw the Trojan goalkeeper reject his attempt. Four clear chances, four failures and an exit in the 70th minute, replaced by Quentin Ndjantou. The contrast is striking with his Parisian debut: after scoring seven goals in his first six appearances, Torres is now going through a series of eight games without scoring.

As a reminder, his last goal dates back to September 20, during the victory against Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1. In the Champions League, he has not found the net since his hat-trick against Slovan Bratislava. Faced with growing questions, Luis Enrique however chose to defend his attacker. Asked at a press conference about his difficulties, the Parisian coach, in fact, wanted to put this less good period into perspective: “everyone was concerned about Mika Godts, now it’s Ferran. These are attackers who miss and score goals.. A protective speech which reflects the technician’s desire not to publicly overwhelm his player.

In the mixed zone, Lucas Beraldo also recalled the importance of solidarity within the Parisian locker room, without wanting to dwell on the individual case of his teammate. “Torres? As I said, every match is different, tonight we played against a very good team, we managed to score and win and that’s the most vital thing. At PSG, we are a family, in good times and in bad times.. Valuable support for the Spaniard, who will now have to quickly regain his effectiveness. Because if Luis Enrique continues to place his trust in him, the missed opportunities begin to accumulate and the shortage becomes difficult to ignore.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10.
  • Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.
  • Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a upcoming Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk said.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone indicates that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the latest year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a significant part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures.
  • Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures.
  • In a recent development, thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

In a recent development, thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

It has been revealed that the table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Industry observers note that sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

Sources indicate that the profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

According to recent reports, ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

It has been revealed that 'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but promptly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Recent findings suggest that salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

Sources indicate that they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

Sources indicate that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ states Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady said that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

In a recent development, intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

Recent findings suggest that city have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

Sources indicate that he utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

Industry observers note that the format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson states, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

By his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

Philippe Diallo is launching into a major battle. The president of the French Football Federation (FFF) has decided to run for the presidency of Fifa, with the ambition of succeeding Gianni Infantino next March. Already supported by UEFA, the French leader is now seeking to convince the various federations. With this in mind, he will travel to Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday, where the General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) will be held.

A trip far from trivial. Philippe Diallo knows it, the African continent constitutes particularly favorable terrain for Gianni Infantino. The outgoing president benefits from significant support, which his opponent intends to try to change. But this strategy is far from unanimous. Industry observers note that the independent journalist, although an opponent of Gianni Infantino, does not mince his words. According to him, Philippe Diallo and certain UEFA officials are completely wrong in their approach to African football. “Either Philippe Diallo is very, very poorly advised, or has he not understood the dynamics of Fifa and international football? His start to the campaign is a sketch since everyone, including several UEFA leaders, is focusing on Africa, which is nonsense, believing that the French-European networks will help (getting 15 votes in Africa would be a victory because it would allow us not to lose the election there). Ideas from another time, with the thought of bringing in well-known people (Africans in particular) to support his campaign and go to large countries with a French-speaking majority (which is the worst possible idea given the arrogance associated with France and UEFA, an elitist association which does not care about “others”)”he believes.

Romain Molina denounces in particular a lack of understanding of the balance of power within international bodies and African federations. The journalist continues his charge by directly implicating the entourage of the president of the FFF. “How can you be so disconnected from reality? However, is this surprising given the recycled “advisors” around him? These people have NO idea of ​​the reality of the federations affiliated to Fifa, and even less of the current dynamics within the confederations/sub-confederations. » A particularly severe first warning for Philippe Diallo, who will have to convince well beyond his European supporters if he wants to shake Gianni Infantino.

Breaking: Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Sources indicate that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Sources indicate that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

In a recent development, the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, mentioned it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

Recent findings suggest that the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

Sources indicate that french Football Weekly: entering the very closed circle of Ballon d’Or winners allowed you to feel fully established among the greatest strikers of all time? Do we need to win this trophy to have the recognition we deserve in the world of football?

According to recent reports, harry Kane: I am extremely proud to have won the Ballon d’Or, and receiving this award in my hometown made the moment even more special. Seeing my name alongside players like R9, who actually gave it to me that evening, Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi and Gerd Müller is an immense source of pride, especially given my journey with loans at the start of my career which forced me to show self-confidence and resilience. Since arriving at Bayern, I have clearly taken a new step, and I feel like I am at the top of my game. I think winning the Ballon d’Or has changed the way people perceive me around the world. I probably underestimated the enthusiasm and the reaction of the fans. When I brandished the trophy in front of the supporters who were waiting for me in the street as I left the ceremony, I understood that I was experiencing a magical moment that I will never forget. This victory is the reflection of an exceptional season that I experienced between the goals, the titles and the great moments. Winning the Ballon d’Or at 33 just highlights that if you continue to work hard and believe in it, you can reach the top.

It has been revealed that FM: Karim Benzema was Ballon d’Or in 2022, Harry Kane was Ballon d’Or in 2026. The full number 9s who participate in the game are highlighted. Do you find any similarities between you and Karim Benzema in your football?

It has been revealed that HK: Karim is an incredible player. I have always been a big admirer of the player. What he achieved at Real Madrid in 2022 was truly impressive. He has this ability to drop into midfield and play almost like a number 10, dictating the play, while arriving in the box at the ideal time. We have slightly different physical characteristics, but in terms of playing intelligence, ability to find spaces and desire to help the players around us, I clearly see a lot of similarities in our football. Both of us demonstrated that it is not always necessary to be in the box to score goals. For me, I have more opportunities when I go lower, because I’m not marked up close. The goals come from me going down and the game developing. I find myself in a number 10 role and, when the opposing block moves back, I shoot from the edge of the area, which is one of my great assets. Last season was the best example: I scored 73 goals, which is almost double the number of goals I scored in any other season.

FM: after winning a Ballon d’Or, what is the priority objective? Go get a second one to make even more history?

According to recent reports, HK: of course, I would love to win another Ballon d’Or, but I know there are many other great players who have their chances. But there are still many trophies I would like to win, like the Champions League with Bayern and, obviously, a title with England.

FM: Last year, your journey in the Champions League ended in the semi-final against PSG after a very high-level double confrontation. Do you think that, this season, Bayern Munich is capable of going for the significant-eared cup?

According to recent reports, HK: the Champions League is a major goal for me and for the team. We have a strong squad, made up of incredible players. Last season, the matches against PSG were crazy, it was decided by a hair, and being eliminated by the team which won the title twice in a row was nothing to be ashamed of. Spending another year with the coach and the team helps us become even stronger. We approached this season telling ourselves that this had to be our year. We have to find a way to achieve this, find that little extra that will make the difference to get through the rounds and do everything we can to win the Champions League. This is our main objective.

FM: You are the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d’Or in over 45 years. Can a player like Michael Olise be your successor, the next Munich player to win this Grail?

In a recent development, HK: Michael is a fantastic player. We see, every day in training, his qualities and what he is capable of doing on the pitch. He undoubtedly has the means to bring a new Ballon d’Or to Munich, that’s for sure.

Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason.

Recent findings suggest that preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office showed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%.

"The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," said Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump.

ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

But economists warned the relief could prove temporary. "Gas and oil prices have risen significantly again in recent weeks," said Stephanie Schoenwald, an economist at Germany's state-owned development bank KfW, citing continuing conflicts and lower inventories.

In a recent development, german President's Frank-Walter Steinmeier latest trip to Asia was intended to provide more clarity. Amid a delicate period, Steinmeier sought a balancing act in China between respect and criticism.

It was a state visit of a kind rarely seen today. For four days, Steinmeier traveled across the country: from Hefei, where the German automaker Volkswagen's China operations are headquartered, through historic villages and the imposing landscapes of the Yellow Mountains. This political balancing act between respect and criticism did not trigger any visible outrage in Beijing.

When he spoke with Chinese leaders about their subsidies for exports to Europe and the related issue of the trade deficit, Xi replied: "I am ready to work together to open a new chapter in the comprehensive strategic partnership between our two countries and to advance the development of global governance.".

Just how much willingness lies behind the push for a strategic partnership will become clear during further negotiations between the EU and China.

Xi Jinping seems to understand that a persistent trade deficit with Europe could also become a problem for his country, as an economic crisis in Europe could further strain China's economy.

As "the world's second- and third-largest economies," China and Germany also bear "an crucial responsibility for the development of relations between China and Europe, as well as for stable growth in the global economy," Xi Jinping said. While that may not sound like a breakthrough yet, it certainly sounds like an understanding.

In contrast to his economic arguments, Steinmeier's political appeals for Beijing to assume more responsibility for the international order fell on deaf ears.

It has been revealed that the German president addressed global conflicts and wars on several occasions in Beijing, including Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine. But he received no responses in official statements.

That same evening, the news channel of the Chinese TV network CCTV aired a report that merely covered Steinmeier's visit to a well-known astrophysics institute.

There was no mention of the call for China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to do more to promote world peace.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.

"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state.".

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

The plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

According to recent reports, munich police mentioned the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ifty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), told the BBC, adding: "Whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories.".

The Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF noted Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

The joint commemoration of the 1958 disaster and the maintenance of the memorial site has produced extensive and friendly relations between Bayern Munich and Manchester United, who will meet in the Champions League in January.

A ban on new Stolpersteine ("stumbling stones") to commemorate victims of the Holocaust in the eastern German town of Heidenau will be upheld after five petitions against the measure were thrown out.

Local councilors from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) voted together in September to pass the controversial ban on newly introduced stones being laid in the town in Saxony, near Dresden.

Petitions against the measure were submitted from across Germany — as well as one from the Netherlands — calling for victims of the Nazi regime to continue to be remembered in Heidenau by way of the small metal plaques embedded in pavements.

"Not everybody has to like the stumbling stones but everyone should have the possibility to lay one in public," one councilor, Michael Schürer, told Germany's Catholic News Agency (KNA), criticizing the rejection of the petitions.

The initiators of the Heidenau ban had argued that, while remembering Holocaust victims remains essential, the placement of Stolpersteine leads to "passersby walking over or even stepping onto the names of the victims." They suggested honoring victims at a local cemetery instead.

The decision of the local Heidenau CDU to join forces with the AfD to pass the motion sparked a nationwide scandal and furthered the debate over the conservatives' commitment to the political "firewall" against the far right.

During his final day of a whirlwind Asia tour this week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul on Friday that Germany and Europe are ready to cooperate with Asian economies to foster a rules-based economic order.

It has been revealed that the UK is the single European signatory, albeit outside of the EU bloc. The US pulled out during the first administration President Donald Trump in 2017, scuttling the original version, the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP).

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is right now in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder Bremen form (all competitions):.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf problem will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip issue, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Centre-forward Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Werder Bremen possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka.

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' overall pattern of results broken.

#25898. Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
